statement: Let n = len(prices), and let s be the minimum of prices[i] + prices[j] over all integer pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i < j < n. The function returns a result r and r = (if s <= money then money - s else money).
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail due to overflow, out-of-bounds access, panic, or any other reason.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= money.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < n and prices[i] + prices[j] <= money, then 0 <= r <= money - 2, and in particular r < money.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the equality r = money holds if and only if for every pair of indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, prices[i] + prices[j] > money.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r < money, there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < n such that prices[i] + prices[j] = money - r.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every pair of indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < n satisfies prices[i] + prices[j] >= money - r.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < n such that prices[i] + prices[j] = money, and for every pair of indices a, b with 0 <= a < b < n, prices[a] + prices[b] >= money.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (prices, money) and returns r' on (prices', money), r = r'.
preconditions: prices and prices' are slices of 64-bit integers of the same length n with 2 <= n <= 50; every entry of prices and of prices' is between 1 and 100; prices' is a reordering (permutation) of the entries of prices; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (prices, money) and returns r' on (prices', money), r' <= r.
preconditions: prices and prices' are slices of 64-bit integers of the same length n with 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100 and 1 <= prices'[i] <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, prices'[i] >= prices[i]; money is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= money <= 100; each of prices and prices' has at least one pair of distinct indices whose sum is at most money.

statement: Let s be the minimum of prices[i] + prices[j] over all 0 <= i < j < n. If s <= money1, and the function returns r1 on (prices, money1) and r2 on (prices, money2), then r2 = r1 + d.
preconditions: prices is a slice of 64-bit integers with n = len(prices) satisfying 2 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= prices[i] <= 100; money1 and money2 are 64-bit integers with 1 <= money1 <= money2 <= 100, and d = money2 - money1.
